prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, half-length demi statue portrait, three-material body: real face and neck, one crystal arm, one stone arm, and a water-filled glass torso ending in a single sealed base at the waist. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to one single, deliberately finished rounded base at her waist, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her waist, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Chinese woman in Hong Kong-style makeup — fair matte skin with a soft powdery finish, thin sharply arched brows, soft brown and rose eyeshadow, a fine black liner with a small flick, long curled lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, a strong rose-red blush on the apples of the cheeks, deep glossy red lips with a defined edge, hair set in glossy voluminous old-film waves, a poised, glamorous expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a large vintage pearl clip earring.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, directly below it a waistline that still pulls in sharply even at this size, then an enormous soft belly of massive rounded folds spilling out beneath it, her left arm made of crystal, her right arm made of carved stone.

Boundary (skin to material, at the collarbones): a single straight, flat line runs around the base of her neck and across both collarbones, nowhere lower, never reaching her chest — never jagged, never zigzag, a clean straight cut like a cross-section, exactly like a clean slice through a cast-glass sculpture. Real skin above this straight line, the material immediately below it. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow. The vessel portion is already full of water right up to this same straight collarbone line and no higher.

Left arm (shoulder to hand): solid transparent crystal, solid clear sea-blue aquamarine crystal, with long fine needle-like tubes at depth and clean facets, deep teal where thickest and pale sea-blue at every thin edge, one continuous carved mass, never hollow, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same crystal. Light passes straight through it; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it.

Right arm (shoulder to hand): carved from ONE solid block of banded black and white onyx, deep glossy black layered with crisp pale cream bands, polished to a hard mirror sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same stone. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface.

Torso (chest and belly, ending at the waist): a sculpted vessel of thick, crystal-clear glass (unmistakably glass: thick, crystal-clear and polished, bright specular reflections, sharp white highlights, tiny trapped bubbles) in the exact shape of her torso, filled completely to the brim with clear citrine-gold water, no hollow space anywhere. Small bright fish and slow-drifting green water plants move freely through the whole filled torso, rising up to the collarbone line itself, never crowding. At her waist, the whole vessel curves inward evenly on every side and seals shut into one single, smooth, rounded base — the vessel simply reaching its natural end there, the one rounded base resting flat on the surface beneath her.

Where each material meets its neighbour (left shoulder, right shoulder), the two distinct materials sit flush against each other with a thin, clean seam, deliberate and precise, never jagged or torn — always the finish of a sculpture, each material keeping its own colour, clarity and surface completely separate from the one beside it.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a warm golden amber on one side and a bright citrus yellow on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: her left hand (crystal) resting at her waist, her right hand (stone) held at chest height clear of her body, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so amber light glances off the left half and citrus light glances off the right half — passing straight through the crystal arm and the glass torso, while only reflecting off the stone arm. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
